volatility.definition: How much and how fast a price swings up and down. High volatility means big jumps in both directions.

drawdown.definition: A fall from a previous high, in percent. After a −50% drawdown the price must rise +100% to get back.

leverage.definition: Investing with borrowed money. It multiplies gains and losses on your own money, and the loan stays even when the investment falls.

risk-capacity.definition: How much money you could lose without it hurting your daily life or your plans.

leading-room.definition: A Korean name for paid chat rooms that sell “sure” stock tips. Regulators warn about them because many are used to hype stocks.

pump-and-dump.definition: Someone buys a stock cheaply, hypes it so others buy and the price rises, then sells. When the buying stops, the price crashes.

diversification.definition: Spreading money over many different investments, so that one failure is only a small part of what you own.

concentration-risk.definition: The risk of having a large share of your money in one place: one company, one sector or one bet.

inflation.definition: Prices rising over time. With 3% inflation, something that costs €100 today costs €103 next year, so the same money buys less.

real-return.definition: What your money earns after inflation. 0.5% interest with 3% inflation is a real return of about −2.5% a year.

compound-interest.definition: Earning interest on earlier interest too. Over long periods it makes growth (and debt) speed up.

emergency-fund.definition: Money kept safe and reachable at once for surprises like a broken machine or a lost job. Often counted in months of costs.

time-horizon.definition: How long until you need the money. The longer it can wait, the more time it has to recover from a fall.

installments.definition: Paying for something in equal parts over several months instead of all at once.

hidden-interest.definition: A cost of borrowing that isn't called interest, such as a cash discount you give up or fees added to a loan.

committed-income.definition: The part of your pay already promised to repayments before the month starts.

revolving-credit.definition: Card debt you roll over from month to month by paying only part of the bill. Interest is charged on what is left.

total-cost-of-credit.definition: The full yearly or monthly cost of a loan with interest, fees and insurance included. In Brazil it is called CET.

home-bias.definition: Investing mostly in your own country because it feels familiar, even when it is a small part of the world.

tax-free-account.definition: An account from the state where gains are not taxed, up to a limit. It changes the tax, not the risk of what is inside.

currency-risk.definition: When you own something priced in another currency, exchange-rate moves change its value in your money, up or down.

rule-of-72.definition: A quick way to guess how fast something doubles. Divide 72 by the yearly rise in %. At 6% a year, prices or savings double in about 12 years.

pay-yourself-first.definition: Moving a fixed amount to savings on the day your pay arrives, before you spend anything. You then spend what is left.
